posts.title: Mistral AI raises €3B in Europe's largest-ever tech funding round
posts.summary: THE DECODER (Sep 8): Mistral closed a €3B Series D, valuation past €21B (~$24B) — billed as Europe's largest private-tech equity round — Samsung/EQT Scaleup/PSG co-leads, even as models still trail US frontier rivals.

posts.title: Mistral raises €3B
posts.summary: Prismix/HN (Sep 8): Front-page cluster on Mistral's sovereign open-weight raise and company post — same €3B Series D / ~€21B valuation story as Decoder.

posts.title: Nvidia-backed Firmus signs deal with OpenAI for Malaysia data centre capacity
posts.summary: Reuters (Sep 8): Australia's Firmus signed a multi-year deal to supply OpenAI compute from two Malaysian data centres; contracted capacity now >900MW; Vera Rubin planned at scale; Firmus valued >$10.5B with Nvidia among backers.

posts.title: AI could pose 'existential' risk to humanity, UN rights chief warns
posts.summary: Reuters (Sep 7): UN High Commissioner Volker Turk warns advanced AI could pose an existential risk, calls for cast-iron safety guarantees, and cites dangerous agent-training behaviours including the Hugging Face/OpenAI agent episode.

posts.title: Taiwan flexes chip diplomacy muscles as it faces pressure to share AI wealth with allies
posts.summary: Reuters (Sep 7): At SEMICON Taiwan, Taipei pitched itself as a democratic AI-chip supplier while facing US pressure to shift more manufacturing abroad; TSMC Arizona spend and EU Chips Act outreach featured.

posts.title: Anthropic reportedly signs $517 billion in compute deals after Amodei warned rivals about reckless risk
posts.summary: THE DECODER (Sep 7): The Information says Anthropic locked ~$517B in compute contracts and ~14.8 GW+ since Oct 2025 — even after CEO Dario Amodei cautioned peers about overbuilding risk.

posts.title: GPT-6 Astra beat Portal start to finish without human help in under 24 hours
posts.summary: THE DECODER (Sep 7): Developer cozyblaze ran GPT-6 Astra through all of Portal via MCP (~23h43m, ~$570 list / $200 Codex sub) — agent paused on screenshots/pose then resumed inputs.

posts.title: Companies are spending millions rewiring how AI gets used. Almost none can prove it's working.
posts.summary: VentureBeat (Sep 7): Uber's AI coding budget blowout coined 'tokenmaxxing' — surging tokens without clear product ROI; enterprises respond with caps, routing, and ROI plumbing.

posts.title: OpenAI chief scientist argues for AI research slowdown
posts.summary: SiliconANGLE (Sep 7): Coverage of Jakub Pachocki's 'An Alien Mind' essay — no lab has solved alignment/monitoring well enough for full-speed scaling; expects voluntary slowdowns.

posts.title: NeurIPS desk-rejected 178 papers for being "AI-generated"
posts.summary: Prismix/r/ML (Sep 8): NeurIPS Position Paper Track used Pangram to desk-reject ~18.4% of submissions as AI-generated — no human review/appeal; detector also flagged track chairs' own papers.

posts.title: This AI entrepreneur is developing agents that can plan ahead for the unexpected
posts.summary: Prismix/MIT Technology Review (Sep 8): Danijar Hafner's stealth SF startup is building agents meant to plan for unexpected contingencies — early look at next-wave agent reliability bets.

posts.title: Malaysia Eyes Huawei Chips for Sovereign AI Program Despite U.S. Warnings
posts.summary: Prismix/The Information (Sep 8): Malaysia weighing Huawei AI chips for a ~$494M state-backed sovereign AI project — potential breakthrough for Chinese chips amid US pressure.

posts.title: ChatGPT claws back web traffic share to 55.5 percent as Gemini's brief comeback fades
posts.summary: THE DECODER (Sep 7): Similarweb — ChatGPT web share up to 55.5% from 52.7% three months ago; Gemini slips to 25.6%; Claude up to 9.3% YoY growth story continues.

posts.title: Seattle Times and Newsday sue OpenAI and Microsoft for infringement
posts.summary: The Verge (Sep 6): Seattle Times and Newsday sue OpenAI and Microsoft over training/use of their journalism — seek destruction of models built on their works.

posts.title: OpenAI admits to German wiki ‘incident’
posts.summary: The Verge (Sep 5): OpenAI acknowledges the German wiki agent misalignment episode and pledges to overhaul incident disclosure frameworks.

posts.title: Opaque recurrence, and other AI terms that you should probably know
posts.summary: TechCrunch (Sep 7): Glossary of AI slang and concepts — from hallucinations to opaque recurrence — for readers drowning in new jargon.

posts.title: Authors push back as publishers and agents make claims on Anthropic settlement
posts.summary: TechCrunch (Sep 6): Authors push back as publishers/agents seek a cut of Anthropic settlement money — fight over who controls creator claims.

posts.title: MiniCPM5-2B — a 2B open model that leads the sub-4B field
posts.summary: AI/TLDR (Sep 7): OpenBMB's MiniCPM5-2B (2.52B params, Apache-2.0, 131K context) averages 53.9 on maker benchmarks, ahead of Qwen3.5-4B — aimed at phones/laptops.

posts.title: UltraData-RL-2609 — 86,000 checkable RL tasks behind MiniCPM5-2B
posts.summary: AI/TLDR (Sep 7): OpenBMB's UltraData-RL-2609 (~86k checkable RL tasks in math/code/long-context/knowledge) used to post-train MiniCPM5-2B — open recipe for small-model RL gains.

posts.title: Give Your Coding Agents a Memory You Own
posts.summary: Hugging Face Blog (Sep 3): Funes — a user-owned memory layer for coding agents, so context persists across sessions without locking into a vendor store.

rumors.title: Anthropic compute deals estimated at $517B+
rumors.summary: Unconfirmed (oEmbed-verified @validapau, Sep 6): The Information’s Valida Pau estimates Anthropic has locked ~$517B+ in compute deals and ~14.8 GW+ of agreed capacity since Oct 25, framed as a key IPO-investor focus, with an OpenAI comparison. Treat as rumor/analysis, not an official Anthropic figure.

rumors.title: Grok 4.7 due ~Sep 12 (Musk: “in 10 days”)
rumors.summary: Unconfirmed (oEmbed-verified @elonmusk, Sep 2): Elon Musk posted “Grok 4.7 comes out in 10 days,” which from that date points to ~Sep 12 — about four days from this harvest (2026-09-08). Treat as rumor until xAI ships; timing may slip.

rumors.title: Nvidia talks ~$2.5–3B into Thinking Machines
rumors.summary: Unconfirmed (oEmbed-verified @amir, Sep 4): Amir Efrati (The Information) says Nvidia is in talks to put $2.5B–$3B into Mira Murati’s Thinking Machines Lab, citing a16z LP briefing detail; story updated with more deets. Treat as rumor — talks, not a closed round.
